newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed steadied by lower harvests.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed steadied by lower harvests.

text.p: Northern Europe rapeseed prices were mostly steadier after confirmation of lower crop figures in Germany and Canada this week, brokers said on Friday.
But they expected bearish pressure later on from USDA's October soybean output report early today, which was above earlier trade estimates.

Statistics Canada on Tuesday put the 1996/97 canola crop at 4.98 million tonnes, down from 6.44 million last year, and the Bonn farm ministry on Wednesday put Germany's 1996 crop at 1.95 million tonnes from 3.11 million in 1995.
"Only small new crop lots appear in the market although buyers are looking hard," one broker said.
"Rape meal prices are also trending higher and oil is still firm," he added.
Brokers also said Polish buying and Scandinavian interest were supportive.
But new crop sunseed was offsetting some of the tightness in rape and crushers were not desperate as processing margins were still unattractive and oil exports subdued.
Oil prices continued to take support from the prospect of possible disruption from consumer opposition to genetically modified U.S. soybeans, which made consumers favour rapeseed.
Environmentalist and consumer groups have expressed health and environmental concerns about the new products.
Nov-Jan rape oil cif Rotterdam was at a $4.25 premium over soy oil at $96.50/100 kg today.
Buyers free Hamburg offered 472.50 marks a tonne for nearby rapeseed, five marks more than a week ago, while Baltic port fob buyers were also five marks up at 475, but sellers were higher.

Rapeseed buyers at German delivery points other than Hamburg pegged October at 447-470 marks, unchanged from a week ago, but raised November ciffo Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp range to 480 from 476 marks previously.
The November position on the Paris Matif futures exchange was last at 463, off seven from last night's close and in quickly expanding volume, in response to the Chicago news.
Local rape meal sellers (34 percent protein) were one mark higher than last week at 30.25 marks/100 kg (Oct) while Nov/Jan meal was at 30.00 (up 0.75).
Oct rape oil was at 85.50 marks/100kg and Nov-Jan oil at 86.00 marks, down one mark from last Friday.
